([[Drexel Hill, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (FL)]] (2019–2023) | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2023]]) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] (2023) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2023) * 2× Third-team All-ACC (2021, 2022) }} '''Isaiah Robert-Johan Wong''' (born January 28, 2001) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). ==High school career== Raised in [[South Brunswick, New Jersey]], Wong played prep basketball at [[Notre Dame High School (New Jersey)|Notre Dame High School]] in [[Lawrenceville, New Jersey]] during his first two years.Fisher, Rich. [https://www.trentonian.com/sports/huge-second-half-pushes-notre-dame-boys-basketball-past-trenton/article_0bfbd5ca-ca74-5ce6-be10-792f3f8aaaf8.amp.html "Huge second half pushes Notre Dame boys basketball past Trenton"], ''[[The Trentonian]]'', January 11, 2016. Accessed May 3, 2021. "Notre Dame also ran a more patient offense after breaking Trenton’s press, as Mike Walley (13 points) hit all three of his 3-pointers after the break. Seniors Sean Hoggs (24) and Troy Jones (23) also benefited from the pace but the true eye-opener was Isaiah Wong, the freshman from South Brunswick, scored 12 of his 21 points in the second half on a variety of penetration moves." For his junior season, he transferred to [[Bonner & Prendergast Catholic High School]] in [[Drexel Hill, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Isaiah Wong Draws A Lot of Attention With His Play |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/07/02/isaiah-wong-draws-a-lot-of-attention-with-his-play/ |website=Dave's Joint |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=July 2, 2018}} As a junior, he averaged 22.2 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game, leading his team to the [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] regular season title, and was named Catholic League MVP.{{cite web |last1=De George |first1=Matthew |title=All-Delco Boys Basketball: Wong finds, conquers his challenge at Bonner & Prendergast |url=https://papreplive.com/2018/04/11/all-delco-boys-basketball-wong-finds-conquers-his-challenge-at-bonner-prendergast/ |website=PA Prep Live |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=April 11, 2018}} In his senior season, Wong averaged 21.9 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game. He led his team to the Class 4A state title game and repeated as Catholic League MVP.{{cite web |last1=De George |first1=Matthew |title=All-Delco Boys Basketball: Repeat season just as good as the first for Bonner's Wong |url=https://papreplive.com/2019/04/19/all-delco-boys-basketball-repeat-season-just-as-good-as-the-first-for-bonners-wong/ |website=PA Prep Live |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=April 19, 2019}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] over offers from [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].{{cite web |last1=Carter |first1=Aaron |title=Bonner-Prendergast's Isaiah Wong commits to the University of Miami |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/isaiah-wong-university-of-miami-commitment-bonner-prendergast-philadelphia-catholic-league-20180926.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=September 26, 2018}} ==College career== On February 9, 2020, Wong recorded a freshman season-high 27 points and 12 rebounds, making all 14 of his free throws, in a 102–95 win over [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] in triple overtime.{{cite web |last1=Stock |first1=Christopher |title=Isaiah Wong's 27-12 leads Miami to 102-95 3OT win over Hokies |url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Isaiah-Wongs-27-12-leads-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-to-102-95-3OT-win-over-Virginia-Tech-Hokies-144090800/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=February 19, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.7 points and three rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Reynolds |first1=John |title=Canes Hoops: Isaiah Wong Profile |url=https://www.stateoftheu.com/2020/11/25/21719552/miami-hurricanes-basketball-isaiah-wong-canes-the-u-jim-larranaga |website=State of the U |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} On January 16, 2021, Wong posted a career-high 30 points, seven rebounds and six assists in a 78–72 victory against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].{{cite web |last1=Stock |first1=Christopher |title=Isaiah Wong's career-high 30 points helps Miami knock off No. 16 Louisville 78-72 |url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Isaiah-Wongs-career-high-30-points-helps-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-knock-off-No-16-Louisville-78-72-159423315/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=January 16, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17.1 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, earning third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] honors.{{cite web |last1=Furones |first1=David |title=UM leading scorer Isaiah Wong announces NBA draft intentions |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-basketball-isaiah-wong-draft-20210414-wcdi72v47ra6xpirvlvb634p4i-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Yero |first1=Michael |title=Isaiah Wong's Breakout Season Shouldn't Be Forgotten |url=https://www.305sports.net/isaiah-wongs-breakout-season-shouldnt-be-forgotten/ |website=305 Sports |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} On April 14, 2021, Wong [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He ultimately returned for his junior season. Wong was named to the third-team All-ACC as a junior.{{cite press release|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |accessdate=March 7, 2022}} He was the second-leading scorer on the team, which advanced to the Elite Eight of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]]. After the season, he again declared for the draft while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite news|first1=Jonathan|last1=Givony|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|title=NIL agent says Miami hoops star Isaiah Wong will enter transfer portal if NIL compensation isn't increased|date=April 28, 2022|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33823826/nil-agent-says-miami-hoops-star-isaiah-wong-enter-transfer-portal-nil-compensation-increased|access-date=April 29, 2022}} In 2023 he was named the ACC player of the year and helped Miami reach their first ever [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]].{{Cite web |title=Hurricanes’ Isaiah Wong named ACC Player of the Year |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-wong-acc-20230306-vobt6tc6wvb4ldspw3alei7wwa-story.html |access-date=2023-04-15 |website=Sun ==Personal life== Wong is the son of Terrence and LaChelle Wong. He has three brothers, named Brian, Terrence and Elijah. His paternal great-grandfather was Chinese.{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Michelle |title=A contract Isaiah Wong signed with his mother is a key to Miami freshman's success |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article240393791.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=February 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118143604/https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article240393791.html|archive-date=January 18, 2021}} In 2022, Wong starred in the short film, 'Top Shot.' {{cite web |last1=Hagani |first1=Alexander |title=Top Shot |url=https://www.alexanderhagani.com/topshot |access-date=June 7, 2023 | date=December 1, 2022| ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://miamihurricanes.com/roster/isaiah-wong/ Miami Hurricanes bio] {{Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Wong, Isaiah}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American sportspeople of Chinese descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Jersey]] [[Category:Miami Hurricanes men's basketball players]] [[Category:Notre Dame High School (New Jersey) alumni]] [[Category:People from Piscataway, New Jersey]] [[Category:People from South Brunswick, New Jersey]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Middlesex County, New Jersey]]
